annotation.evidence_span: unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.
annotation.interpretation_a: The endpoint is allowed to send packets from a different local address if it has *received* and processed a preferred_address parameter.
annotation.interpretation_b: The endpoint is allowed to send packets from a different local address if it has *sent* a preferred_address parameter.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'acted on' is vague. It could mean either receiving and processing the preferred_address parameter (implying the peer has indicated a preferred address), or sending the preferred_address parameter (implying the endpoint has requested a preferred address). These have different implications for when the endpoint is permitted to send packets from a different local address.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether 'acted on' means receiving and processing the parameter, or sending it. This affects whether the endpoint can use a different local address after sending a preferred_address parameter but before receiving a response.
